analysis:
This PR changes only the public landing site. In landing/src/content/pricing.ts lines 48 and 51, Markdown links now point to /developers.md instead of /developers. In landing/src/content/public-site.ts line 4, publicPagePaths drops /developers and /contact, so they leave the sitemap and canonical page list. The tests in landing/tests/*.mjs are updated to match: retired HTML routes should return 404, while the .md twins and Accept-negotiated Markdown stay available. None of this touches the provider, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, prefix cache (T-041) or fan helper. I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 or TB-011 or their threats.

The public privacy text (publicFacts.privacy, line 11) is unchanged. It still states hop-by-hop encryption and that the provider is the plaintext endpoint, so there is no new overclaim. The pricing fetch is unchanged. It uses an env-overridable API base (line 19), a 5s timeout and strict validation of the price fields. It still replaces |, \r and \n in model names (line 50), which limits Markdown table injection. No auth header is sent and no new data exposure is introduced.

One limit: the routing and middleware code that actually implements the 404 for retired HTML pages, the Markdown negotiation and the page removals is not in the supplied batch. The tests assert this behavior, but I could not verify it. Even so, any gap there would be a site-availability or content-negotiation issue, not a threat-model asset. The unseen edits to the llms.txt, index.md and auth.md generators and to the page components that removed the links should be checked in another pass for accuracy.
